_help.about: [NOT WIRED YET — design §CR] The world at 1/100 Earth (Mike, 3 Oct): shrink the gaps, not the things. Planet size, terrain heights, the great ranges, walking pace on slopes, and biome shares. First guesses by Claude (chat), 3 Oct; the designer owns them. Reference maths: tools/reference/world_scale_reference.py.
_help.planet: circumference_m: the planet actually built (400 km is 1/100 Earth; the 1/10 planet was 4,000 km). It equals the geography's layout size (PlanetConst.GEO_CIRCUMFERENCE_M), so the layout is built at its own size (GEO_SCALE 1). It is a data value so the two sizes can be compared in play (the horizon, §CR). things_true_size: everything at walking scale (people, folk, creatures, plants, ruins, camps) keeps its real size; only the gaps between things shrink.
_help.heights: height_scale: terrain heights as a share of Earth's, unchanged at 0.1 (an Everest-class summit is about 885 m). Altitude bands, the lapse rate and the cloud layers keep following it (CloudLayers: the low deck sits at 50-200 m, so the great summits stand above it).
_help.mountains: great_ranges: how many per world. summit_m_earth: their summits in Earth metres (times height_scale in the game). route_mean_deg / route_max_deg: every great summit, or its high pass, has a walkable route (ridge, valley or switchbacks) this steep on average and at most. cliff_min_deg: ground steeper than this is a sheer face. cliff_share: the share of mountain flank area that is sheer; sheer faces are barriers, since this game has no wall climbing (§AT). footprint_max: how many times their honest share of ground the great ranges may take, the one exception to honest shares, so their routes keep real angles at 1/10 heights. walk_max_deg: ground steeper than this can't be walked up.
_help.pace: Walking up and down slopes follows Tobler's hiking function, scaled to the flat walk: factor = exp(-a * |s + b|) / exp(-a * b), where s is rise over run, capped at max_factor (1.0 means no downhill boost). It applies to walking and sprinting. flat_walk_mps: the ambient walk it scales (from movement.json; read here only for the reference maths). climb_target_game_h: a great summit from its foot (the reference maths: a 500 m summit by a 20° route about 3.4 game hours, an 885 m one about 6, or 7 by 25°).
_help.biome_shares: honest: each land biome covers its Earth share of land. floor_places / floor_km2: a biome that would get fewer places than this gets this many, each at least this big, so the small niche biomes can be found. earth_reference: Earth's shares by biome, filled with sources once the engine reports what the generator makes at 1/100 (null until then).
_help.horizon_reference: Read-only numbers from the reference maths, for Mike: metres to the horizon and how far tall things show, on this planet and on the 1/10 one. The game doesn't read them.
